messages:
Asha (oncall): seeing a spike in pod restarts in us-west-2 — multiple serving-runtime replicas crash with CUDA illegal memory access followed by OOM. Raising incident.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-2026-0412-78 — severity: P1. Pager notified.

Liam (sre): copy of `kubectl get pods -n inference` shows CrashLoopBackOff / OOMKilled. Small sample: 
```
NAME                                    READY   STATUS             RESTARTS   AGE
serving-runtime-5f7d9c8b-rc1k          0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   12         2h
serving-runtime-5f7d9c8b-rc2m          0/1     OOMKilled          5          1h
serving-runtime-canary-1                1/1     Running            0          18m
```

Liam (sre): attaching recent container logs (short):
```
[2026-04-12T09:17:03Z] runtime: invoking model shard 3
[2026-04-12T09:17:04Z] runtime: nvcrash: kernel reported illegal memory access at 0x7f8b12c4
[2026-04-12T09:17:04Z] launcher: aborting shard - exit status 137 (SIGKILL)
```

Priya (eng-runtime): can we get `dmesg` / kernel logs from the host? This smells like a device address translation / pagewalk misalignment. If it's the kernel driver or SMMU, we'll need kernel team.

josh (infra): grabbing dmesg, short snippet: 
```
[ 1123.456789] nvidia: device 0000:86:00.0: GPU: device addr fault, VA=0x7f8b12c4, misaligned-address
[ 1123.456792] aperfmperf: collected metrics
[ 1123.457001] oom-killer: kill process 14567 (server) score 123 or sacrifice child
```

Priya (eng-runtime): thanks. That misaligned-address line fits the kernel-level misaligned device address reports we've seen in the past. Could be a pagewalk race where the kernel's pfn->dma mapping gets a stale translation.

Asha (oncall): customer impact — Support Team, please confirm which customers are impacted and whether it's affecting avatars/batches/real-time. @Support Team

Support Team: two customers with elevated error rates — one batch job failing entirely (customers/customer-42), one small real-time tenant seeing latency spikes and 5xx (customers/customer-99). Link to query: http://splunk.redwood.example/query/INC-2026-0412-78

Liam (sre): immediate mitigation plan: 1) route traffic off failing nodes (cordon + drain); 2) route a portion of live traffic to a stable model variant (quantized smaller variant) as a fallback; 3) collect kernel + nvcrash dumps and escalate.

Priya (eng-runtime): implementing fallback routing now. Running redwood route commands: 
```
# cut 80% from standard pool -> canary pool
redwood route update inference --from=serving-runtime --to=serving-runtime-canary --percent=20
```

kubectl-bot: Node cordon/evacuation started for node gpu-node-5 by josh.

josh (infra): cordoned gpu-node-5, draining pods. Observed two pods successfully rescheduled to other nodes; one failed due to imagePull backoff (unrelated).

Priya (eng-runtime): canary variant is up (serving-runtime-canary-1). Canary uses `gpt-3l-quant` (different allocator & quantized kernels) — initial 20% shifted. Monitoring logs.

Liam (sre): monitoring shows reduced 5xx from 68% -> 22% within 6 minutes of routing change. Good signal. Keep scaling canary slowly.

Priya (eng-runtime): stack trace from nvcrash dump (excerpt):
```
# nvcrash excerpt
GPUMemCopy: attempt to copy from device addr 0x7f8b12c4 -> mapped pfn mismatch
Backtrace: handle_ioctl+0x1a3, gpu_submit+0x204, vm_page_fault+0x2f4
Warning: possible concurrent pte update during pagewalk
```

Priya (eng-runtime): this strongly suggests a race in pagewalker / pfn -> dma mapping on the host. Not an immediate fix in runtime code. Kernel/driver patch required or temporary workaround: avoid the allocation pattern triggering the path (use small contiguous allocations, or pin pages differently).

Asha (oncall): handoff — I'm going offline in 30m. Handover to @Priya for engineering follow-up and to @Liam for SRE actions (cordon/drain bookkeeping). Anyone else?

Liam (sre): noted. I'll keep watch on reschedules and eviction churn. Filing escalation to kernel-driver team: KR-2026-158.

incident-bot: Escalation ticket created: KR-2026-158 — kernel/driver team assigned.

Priya (eng-runtime): temporary runtime change to reduce exposure: disable large prefetch in allocator (flip `ENABLE_PREFETCH=0`) on canary and restart. Command: 
```
docker exec -it runtime-canary bash -c 'export ENABLE_PREFETCH=0 && svc restart runtime'
```

josh (infra): infra note — we restarted kubelet on gpu-node-5 after draining; node came back healthy but we'll keep it cordoned until kernel patch.

Support Team: customers notified via status page and targeted emails. Customer-42 job rerun recommended after node drains.

kubectl-bot: Canary routing update: 20% -> 60% -> 100% over 25 minutes. No repeat crashes observed on canary variant.

Priya (eng-runtime): logs look stable on quantized variant. However, if we rerun heavy seq-length workloads on standard runtime path we still reproduce on drained hosts previously.

Liam (sre): next ops steps: keep node cordoned, gather full nvcrash + kernel dump (already started s3 upload), keep canary at full traffic until patch. Prepare rollback playbook if canary shows any regressions.

Asha (oncall): thanks team. Assigning postmortem: Priya will own root-cause analysis and remediation plan; include kernel team. I'll add a timeline and customer impact summary.

Priya (eng-runtime): acknowledged. Immediate tickets: INC-2026-0412-78 (this incident), KR-2026-158 (kernel escalation), POST-2026-0412 (postmortem).

Liam (sre): flag for follow-up: add an automated check to detect `misaligned-address` dmesg patterns and automatically shift traffic to guarded canary.

Asha (oncall): closing out on-call rotation — keep triage channel open for updates. If kernel patch lands, we'll schedule a controlled rollout and test on a canary node set first.

Support Team: marking incident as "mitigated" for customer comms. Will update status page with details and ETA for permanent fix. :white_check_mark:

Asha (oncall): logging end-of-thread notes here for postmortem. Thanks all — great coordination.
